title: Oscars Visual Effects Top 20 Revealed: Disney Leads With Four Titles as ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘Ramayana,’ ‘Dune: Part Three’ and ‘Wildwood’ Make the Cut (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Oscars VFX 20-film shortlist favors Disney, boosting visibility for actors in effects-driven releases.
content: Other VFX finalists include “Backrooms,” “Digger,” “Godzilla Minus Zero,” “The Mosquito Bowl,” “Project Hail Mary” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” The Oscar race for visual effects is down to 20, and the road to the 99th Academy Awards runs through Ithaca, Motunui and a galaxy far, far away. The Academy’s Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Through multiple sources, Variety has confirmed all 20 of the finalists, including Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three,” Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s “Project Hail Mary,” Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day” and Marvel Studios’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” from Anthony and Joe Russo. Related Stories 'The Body' Debuts With 5.1 Million Views in Five Days 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir The Academy does not release the top 20 externally and declines to comment or confirm which films advanced. Disney leads the confirmed titles with four. Alongside “Avengers: Doomsday,” the studio lands Jon Favreau’s “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” 20th Century Studios’ “Whalefall” and Thomas Kail’s live-action “Moana,” which brings Dwayne Johnson back as the demigod Maui. Skydance (formerly Warner Bros. Discovery) took three of the spots: “Dune: Part Three,” Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Tom Cruise-led “Digger” and Craig Gillespie’s “Supergirl” from former DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran. But the studio also sees four contenders fall short. Villeneuve’s stakes are historic. Both “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two” won the visual effects Oscar, and in March, “Avatar: Fire and Ash” made James Cameron’s franchise three-for-three in the category. “Dune: Part Three,” which opens Dec. 18, now puts Villeneuve two steps from the same trilogy sweep. title: The Top 21 New Movies Streaming Now
summary: November streaming drops spotlight major new films, offering fresh visibility for featured talent across platforms.
content: Nicolas Cage as John Madden, a Jessica Chastain thriller and the biggest horror movie of the year hit streaming in November If you’re looking for a great new movie to watch on streaming, you’ve come to the right place. November has a host of new movies hitting your favorite streaming service, including some high profile films just in time for the holidays. We’ve gone through and made a curated list of the best new movies added to Netflix , Prime Video , HBO Max , Hulu and more this month. They include a “Madden” biopic starring Nicolas Cage, a Netflix thriller starring Jessica Chastain, a pair of Oscar contenders and a new streaming home for “Obsession.” Rian Johnson is one of our best living filmmakers, and “Looper” is one of his very best films. This original sci-fi movie stars Joseph Gordon-Levitt as an assassin living in the future who offs people who are sent back in time by his crime syndicate in the future, thus getting rid of all evidence. But when his latest target turns out to be his future self (played by Bruce Willis), things take a turn. Emily Blunt co-stars in this sharp, emotional and terrifying vision of the future. This new film, based on a novel by “A Dog’s Purpose” author W. Bruce Cameron, is described by Netflix as “a tale of a family in crisis where a teenager, her grandfather and his trusty basset hound struggle to keep the household together at Christmas.” The film was directed by Cathryn Michon, who had previously worked on the movie versions of “A Dog’s Purpose” and “A Dog’s Journey” with Cameron. title: How 'Backrooms' Artisans Transformed YouTube Series Into Cinema’s Favorite Liminal Space Using 30,000 Square Feet of Sets and Four Sound Stages
summary: Backrooms expands from YouTube to large-scale studio sets, signaling opportunities in viral-to-film projects for adaptable performers.
content: Before Kane Parsons’ “ Backrooms ” became a $400 million global box office success, it was a YouTube series with 22 episodes, each ranging from two minutes to 45 minutes exploring the “Backrooms” lore. The series was a viral hit, and so was the movie. However, for the film’s production designer Danny Vermette and visual effects supervisor Ed Douglas, neither was initially aware of the series. After receiving a call from the film’s producer, Chris Ferguson, both Douglas and Vermette went down the rabbit hole and dove right in. Related Stories Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Star in Netflix’s 'The Twilight Between Us' From 'When Life Gives You Tangerines' Director, 'Queen of Tears' Writer Penelope Cruz to Star in and Produce Netflix Drama 'Patricia' From 'On the Fringes' Director Juan Diego Botto Speaking with Variety, Douglas, whose work is shortlisted for Oscar consideration , recalled his first response: “Is this real? Is this CG? What is this going to be?” After jumping on a call with Parsons, he learned about how the world had been built using Blender, 3D creation software used for modeling, animation, CGI, rendering, visual effects and simulation.” He says, “We started talking about what our process would be. Would this be a very traditional, film VFX process or would we bring in a hybrid process with the Kane Parsons Blender workflow? It was that combined process that we built.” Set in 1991, the film stars Chiwetel Ejiofor as Clark, a furniture emporium owner who discovers a portal in the basement of his store. Clark becomes obsessed with this alternate world, a never-ending series of liminal spaces lined with carpet and yellow wallpaper. title: Cult Hit 'Hundreds of Beavers' Returns to Theaters for Big Christmas Expansion
summary: Cult indie Hundreds of Beavers gets wider Christmas theatrical rollout, increasing exposure for its cast and creators.
content: It’s been four years since the cult hit “ Hundreds of Beavers ” first debuted and still two years since it started really gaining traction with wider audiences in 2024. But if it feels like the black and white, silent, slapstick indie comedy still hasn’t left the cultural conversation , that’s because in all that time it has continued to quietly play in theaters and attract audiences both loyal and new alike. Technically, “Hundreds of Beavers” has never left theaters. It continues to play individual screenings in a city or two every weekend. Now, though, “Hundreds of Beavers” is set to return to theaters for what is its biggest theatrical expansions to date. The film will kick off its third annual Northwoods Christmas, which will feature 130 screenings across 85 cities, with more to likely be added in the coming weeks. It came about after another fan campaign pushed for the film to come to some markets it hadn’t previously thought about or targeted such as Indianapolis and Charlottesville, and it will now play in everything from concert venues to microcinemas. Related Stories Cinematographer Caleb Deschanel on Finding the Right Techniques For ‘The Right Stuff’ Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? The re-releases have become a holiday tradition for “Hundreds of Beavers,” which for all its wintery setting and its main character dressed like Santa, is being positioned as a new Christmas movie. The first time “Hundreds of Beavers” was re-released at Christmas 2024, which was shortly after the Blu-ray for the film became available, it brought in $118K at the box office in a month, and the producers continued the tradition in 2025. “There’s room for a Christmas tradition with the energy of a ‘Rocky Horror’ screening,” said producer Kurt Ravenwood. “You can watch ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ and ‘White Christmas’ all you want, but for getting together with friends and family to laugh about the miserable winter ahead, ‘Hundreds of

Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in 'The Further Mis-Adventures of
 Cliff Booth'?
summary: Tarantino's new Cliff Booth installment sidelines Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate, hinting future adaptations may center on Booth.
content: [Editor’s note: This article contains small spoilers for “ The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .”] It should come as little surprise that David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” focuses on, well, Cliff Booth. The Quentin Tarantino -penned sequel to the filmmaker’s own 2019 Oscar-winning hit “ Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ” has always been billed as a spinoff following the continuing adventures of his fictitious (yet still iconic) stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). But Tarantino has always loved building out his own shared and connected universe (s), and fans sure love exploring its outer limits. “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and, by extension, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” occupy a unique place in Tarantino’s cinematic world, as they’re both part of his so-called “Realer Than Real World Universe” and his “Movie Movie Universe.” Tarantino didn’t just keep crafting his movies-within-movies world with the hit film — he also introduced real-world (realer than real world?) elements and people (the Manson Family, of course, and all that entails). Related Stories ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March ‘The Trip’ Returns for Fifth Installment, Next Sending Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon to Frigid Arctic Circle That bent continues in “Cliff Booth,” which is rife with both out-there elements and very real references (time for that “Hee Haw” resurgence, we guess). But the film also has to follow its own series logic, which means, yes, it’s the Cliff Booth show, but hey, where are our “Hollywood” co-stars Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie)? [Once again: This article contains small spoilers for “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”] When we first meet Cliff and Rick, the duo are long-time colleagues and best pals. title:
GloRilla to Make Acting Debut in Deon Taylor's Horror-Thriller 'Don't
 Open the Door,' Starring Armani Greer (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: GloRilla’s acting debut in Deon Taylor’s Don't Open the Door signals new casting opportunities and crossover visibility for performers.
content: Grammy-nominated rapper GloRilla will make her acting debut in the upcoming movie “Don’t Open the Door.” Armani Greer (“Why Did I Get Married Again?” “The Drop: A Snowfall Saga”) is confirmed to star in the film, described as an “elevated horror-thriller” from writer-director Deon Taylor (“Traffik,” “Black and Blue,” “The Intruder,” “Meet the Blacks”). The project is the latest film from Deon Taylor and Roxanne Avent Taylor’s independent studio, Hidden Empire Film Group. Related Stories 'Grendel' Animated Series Set at Netflix From 'Widow's Bay' Writer Years After Live-Action Adaptation Was Scrapped U2 Salutes Dolly Parton With Recreation of Their 'Torn' Duet in NFL Thanksgiving Eve Halftime Show “Hidden Empire was built on taking the bolder swing, and this cast is our clearest example yet,” said Taylor, announcing the two major castings. “Pairing Armani with GloRilla in her acting debut gave us something audiences haven’t seen before. You can’t fake that kind of energy, and I can’t wait for people to feel it.” Greer and GloRilla (aka Gloria Hallelujah Woods) are the latest to join the cast alongside Tyrese Gibson (the “Fast & Furious” and “Transformers” franchises), Ron Livingston (“The Conjuring,” “Office Space”), Beverly D’Angelo (“National Lampoon’s Vacation” franchise, “American History X”) and Omar Benson Miller (“Sinners,” “Ballers”). Production is currently underway in Mississippi, with Maxime Alexandre (“The Nun,” “Annabelle: Creation,” “Crawl”) on board as the film’s cinematographer. Plot details are being kept under wraps, with filmmakers only revealing that the film “focuses on real-world trauma.” The “Don’t Open the Door” movie is also intended to launch a graphic novel-inspired universe that pushes the story beyond the screen. title: What Are Local Movie Theaters Showing for Thanksgiving 2026?
summary: Thanksgiving 2026 programming favors family franchises and prestige titles, guiding actors’ release strategies and holiday promotional planning.
content: One of the great things about going to the movies by yourself is that, technically speaking, you’re not alone. Even if you’re the only person in the auditorium, somebody thought about what you might like to watch, put it on the calendar, and made sure there was a place for you to sit. Earlier this month, IndieWire surveyed the programming at independent movie theaters across the United States on Election Night . Continuing that exercise over Thanksgiving weekend reveals another delightful cross-section of American film culture — albeit with considerably more cannibalism. Related Stories ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen? Watch ‘The Sheep Detectives’ VFX Supervisor Break Down the ‘Sheep-Isms’ That Made His Characters Stand Out At the Music Box Theatre in Chicago , where audiences have spent more than two decades celebrating Thanksgiving by singing along to “The Sound of Music,” moviegoers can also catch Ruggero Deodato’s “Cannibal Holocaust” late Friday night. It’s hard to imagine the Von Trapps sticking around for that one, but there’s something lovely about a neighborhood institution accommodating both crowds. In Seattle, the Beacon is observing its own Thanksgiving tradition with “Blood Rage,” the gloriously ridiculous slasher that made cranberry sauce an enduring point of reference for a certain subset of horror fans. For a somewhat more realistic depiction of the horrors of going home for Thanksgiving, SALA Event Center in Los Alamos, New Mexico , is showing Jodie Foster’s “Home for the Holidays.” In Cambridge, Massachusetts, the Brattle Theatre is celebrating Black Friday with a double feature of “Chopping Mall” and “Night of the Comet.” If you’d rather watch people die in a shopping mall than go to one yourself, that’s certainly an economical alternative.
